faqs.q: When can bats be excluded from a Boca Raton home?
faqs.a: Bat exclusion is legal in Florida from August 15 through April 15. Excluding or blocking bats during maternity season, April 16 through August 14, is illegal under FWC Rule 68A-9.010. The house bats here are Brazilian free-tailed and evening bats. In maternity season our crew can inspect, identify the roost, and schedule the exclusion for the legal window — and a bat found in a room with a sleeping person is a county health department call first.

faqs.q: We feed a Lake Worth Beach cat colony — how does that affect raccoon problems?
faqs.a: Directly: outdoor cat food is raccoon food on a schedule, and it is the single most common driver of the city's raccoon density around homes. Managed colonies do best with measured feeding — food out briefly, then removed — which keeps cats fed and raccoons uninvited. We will never trap indiscriminately near a colony; our plans identify feeding stations, schedule around them, and target the attic animals specifically. The colony and the exclusion can coexist; the buffet and the exclusion cannot.
